questions.stem: Who is the author of the autobiography 'Wings of Fire'?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) is the autobiography of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, India's 11th President and 'Missile Man', co-written with Arun Tiwari. It covers his early life, his work at ISRO and DRDO, and India's missile programme. Kalam's other books include 'India 2020', 'Ignited Minds', and 'Turning Points'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'Discovery of India' was written by:
questions.explanation: 'The Discovery of India' was written by Jawaharlal Nehru during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort (1942–46). It traces Indian history, philosophy, and culture from the Indus Valley Civilisation onwards. It was later adapted into the TV series 'Bharat Ek Khoj' by Shyam Benegal. Nehru also wrote 'Glimpses of World History' and 'An Autobiography (Toward Freedom)'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote the classic economics treatise 'The Wealth of Nations'?
questions.explanation: 'An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations' (1776) by Adam Smith is the foundational text of modern economics. It introduced the 'invisible hand' concept and arguments for free markets and division of labour. Smith is called the 'Father of Economics'. Marx wrote 'Das Kapital'; Keynes wrote 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Sanskrit play 'Abhijnanasakuntalam' (The Recognition of Shakuntala) was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Abhijnanasakuntalam' is the masterpiece of Kalidasa, the greatest Sanskrit poet and dramatist (often called the 'Shakespeare of India'), who flourished in the Gupta period. His other works include 'Meghaduta', 'Raghuvamsha', 'Kumarasambhava', and 'Vikramorvashiyam'. Banabhatta wrote 'Harshacharita'; Vishakhadatta wrote 'Mudrarakshasa'; Sudraka wrote 'Mrichchhakatika'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who authored the famous treatise 'Arthashastra' on statecraft and economics?
questions.explanation: 'Arthashastra' was written by Chanakya (also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta), the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya. It is an ancient treatise on statecraft, economic policy, military strategy, and administration. Rediscovered in 1905 by R. Shamasastry, it reveals sophisticated Mauryan governance. Panini wrote 'Ashtadhyayi' (Sanskrit grammar); Patanjali wrote the 'Yoga Sutras'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The novel 'Gitanjali', for which its author won the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913), was written by:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali' (Song Offerings) — the first non-European and first Indian to win a Nobel. Tagore also wrote India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and Bangladesh's 'Amar Sonar Bangla'. Bankim Chandra wrote 'Anandamath' (containing 'Vande Mataram').
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote 'The God of Small Things', which won the Booker Prize in 1997?
questions.explanation: 'The God of Small Things' (1997) by Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in 1997. It is set in Kerala and explores the lives of twins Rahel and Estha. Kiran Desai won the Booker in 2006 for 'The Inheritance of Loss'. Other Indian-origin Booker winners include Salman Rushdie ('Midnight's Children', 1981) and Aravind Adiga ('The White Tiger', 2008).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the first Education Minister of independent India and a prominent freedom fighter. His birthday (11 November) is celebrated as National Education Day. The book gives an insider account of the freedom struggle and Partition. Azad was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1992.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who is the author of 'A Brief History of Time', a landmark work of popular science?
questions.explanation: 'A Brief History of Time' (1988) by physicist Stephen Hawking explains cosmology — the Big Bang, black holes, and the nature of time — for a general audience. It became an international bestseller. Hawking also wrote 'The Universe in a Nutshell' and 'The Grand Design'. Carl Sagan wrote 'Cosmos'; Feynman wrote 'Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The epic 'Mahabharata' is traditionally attributed to:
questions.explanation: The 'Mahabharata', the longest epic poem in the world (~100,000 verses), is traditionally attributed to the sage Ved Vyasa (Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa). It contains the Bhagavad Gita. The 'Ramayana' is attributed to Valmiki. Tulsidas wrote the 'Ramcharitmanas' (Awadhi retelling of the Ramayana). Vyasa is also credited with compiling the Vedas and the Puranas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote 'The Argumentative Indian', a collection of essays on Indian history and identity?
questions.explanation: 'The Argumentative Indian' (2005) was written by Nobel laureate economist Amartya Sen (Economics, 1998). The book explores India's tradition of debate, heterodoxy, and pluralism. Sen also wrote 'Development as Freedom' and 'The Idea of Justice'. Raghuram Rajan (former RBI Governor) wrote 'I Do What I Do' and 'Fault Lines'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule), outlining a critique of modern civilisation, was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Hind Swaraj' (1909) was written by Mahatma Gandhi in Gujarati aboard a ship from London to South Africa. It presents his philosophy of self-rule, non-violence, and critique of Western industrial civilisation, in a dialogue format. Gandhi's autobiography is 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'. Tilak wrote 'Gita Rahasya'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who authored 'The Origin of Species', the foundational work of evolutionary biology?
questions.explanation: 'On the Origin of Species' (1859) by Charles Darwin introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection. It is one of the most influential scientific books ever written. Darwin also wrote 'The Descent of Man' (1871). Alfred Russel Wallace co-discovered natural selection; Mendel founded genetics; Thomas Huxley ('Darwin's Bulldog') was a key defender of evolution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'Geetanjali Shree's 'Tomb of Sand' (Ret Samadhi) made history in 2022 by becoming:
options: The first Hindi novel to win the International Booker Prize
The first Indian novel to win the Pulitzer Prize
The first Tamil novel to win the Nobel Prize
The best-selling Indian novel of all time
questions.explanation: 'Tomb of Sand' (originally 'Ret Samadhi' in Hindi) by Geetanjali Shree, translated by Daisy Rockwell, won the International Booker Prize in 2022 — the first Hindi-language and first South Asian language novel to win. The International Booker honours translated fiction, with the £50,000 prize split equally between author and translator.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote the political satire 'Animal Farm' and the dystopian novel '1984'?
questions.explanation: George Orwell (pen name of Eric Arthur Blair) wrote 'Animal Farm' (1945), an allegory of the Russian Revolution, and '1984' (1949), a dystopia introducing concepts like 'Big Brother', 'doublethink', and 'thoughtcrime'. Aldous Huxley wrote 'Brave New World'; Ray Bradbury wrote 'Fahrenheit 451' — both also famous dystopias.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The famous work 'Raghuvamsha', an epic poem on the dynasty of Lord Rama, was composed by:
questions.explanation: 'Raghuvamsha' (The Dynasty of Raghu) is a Sanskrit mahakavya (epic poem) by Kalidasa, describing the kings of the Raghu dynasty including Lord Rama. Bharavi wrote 'Kiratarjuniya'; Magha wrote 'Shishupala Vadha'; Sriharsha wrote 'Naishadhacharita'. These, with Kalidasa's 'Kumarasambhava', form part of the celebrated Sanskrit mahakavyas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who is the author of 'Playing It My Way', an autobiography by a famous Indian cricketer?
questions.explanation: 'Playing It My Way' (2014) is the autobiography of Sachin Tendulkar, the 'Master Blaster' and the only cricketer with 100 international centuries. It set a record for pre-publication bookings for an adult hardback. Tendulkar received the Bharat Ratna in 2014, becoming the first sportsperson to receive India's highest civilian honour.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'Panchatantra', a collection of animal fables, was compiled by:
questions.explanation: 'Panchatantra' (Five Treatises) is an ancient collection of interrelated animal fables in Sanskrit, traditionally attributed to Vishnu Sharma (c. 3rd century BCE). Written to teach princes the wisdom of statecraft (niti), it spread worldwide and influenced fables like Aesop's. Somadeva wrote 'Kathasaritsagara'; Dandin wrote 'Dashakumaracharita'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote the book 'The Inheritance of Loss', winner of the 2006 Booker Prize?
questions.explanation: 'The Inheritance of Loss' (2006) by Kiran Desai won the Booker Prize in 2006. Set in Kalimpong (West Bengal) and New York, it deals with colonialism, globalisation, and identity. Kiran is the daughter of novelist Anita Desai (thrice Booker-shortlisted). Jhumpa Lahiri won the Pulitzer for 'Interpreter of Maladies' (2000).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The treatise 'Indica', describing Mauryan India, was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Indica' was written by Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra. Though the original is lost, fragments survive in later Greek writers (Arrian, Strabo, Diodorus). Fa-Hien and Hiuen Tsang were Chinese Buddhist pilgrims; Al-Biruni wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' during Mahmud of Ghazni's era.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the author to a work they did NOT write. Who among these did NOT write the work attributed to them?
options: V.S. Naipaul — 'The God of Small Things'
questions.explanation: The incorrect pairing is option D: 'The God of Small Things' was written by Arundhati Roy, NOT V.S. Naipaul. Naipaul (Nobel laureate, 2001) wrote 'A House for Mr Biswas' and 'A Bend in the River'. The other three pairings are correct: Vikram Seth–'A Suitable Boy', Rushdie–'Midnight's Children', R.K. Narayan–'Malgudi Days'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', which developed the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, was written by:
questions.explanation: 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) was written by Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', who systematically developed the 'Drain of Wealth' theory — that Britain was draining India's wealth through unfair economic policies. Naoroji was the first Asian elected to the British House of Commons. R.C. Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who wrote 'Rajatarangini', a historical chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, regarded as one of India's earliest works of history-writing?
questions.explanation: 'Rajatarangini' (River of Kings), composed in Sanskrit verse by Kalhana in the 12th century (c. 1148–49), chronicles the dynasties of Kashmir. It is notable for its relatively critical, chronological approach to history — rare in ancient Indian literature. Jonaraja later wrote a continuation. Bilhana wrote 'Vikramankadevacharita'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Persian-language memoir 'Tuzuk-i-Baburi' (Baburnama) was written by:
options: Babur (in Chagatai Turkic, later translated to Persian)
questions.explanation: The 'Baburnama' (Tuzuk-i-Baburi) is the autobiography of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire, originally written in Chagatai Turkic and later translated into Persian during Akbar's reign. Abul Fazl wrote 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari'; Gulbadan Begum (Babur's daughter) wrote 'Humayun-nama'. Jahangir wrote his own memoir, 'Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which book authored by an RBI Governor offers a critique of global financial systems and warned of the 2008 financial crisis?
options: 'The Future of India' by Bimal Jalan
'Through the Looking Glass' by D. Subbarao
questions.explanation: 'Fault Lines: How Hidden Fractures Still Threaten the World Economy' (2010) by Raghuram Rajan won the Financial Times/Goldman Sachs Business Book of the Year. Rajan had warned of systemic financial risks at the 2005 Jackson Hole conference, before the 2008 crisis. He served as RBI Governor (2013–16). Urjit Patel's 'Overdraft' and D. Subbarao's 'Who Moved My Interest Rate?' are other RBI Governor memoirs.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
